intro.title: Optimistic UI
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple todo list app that updates instantly when you add new items, even before the server confirms the change. You'll learn how to implement Optimistic UI, a pattern that makes apps feel faster by showing expected changes immediately. We'll use React's useState hook to manage the todo list state and simulate API calls with setTimeout. By the end, you'll understand how to create responsive interfaces that provide better user experience by assuming success while handling potential errors gracefully.
intro.usecase: Optimistic UI is a crucial pattern in modern web applications where immediate feedback is expected. You'll see this in social media platforms when liking a post—the heart icon instantly turns red while the request processes in the background. E-commerce sites use it when adding items to cart, showing the item count update immediately before confirming with the server. Form submissions in dashboards often display success states optimistically, making the interface feel snappier and more responsive to user actions.
